question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of an untreated liver hydatid cyst?

options.A: Rupture into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Biliary tract obstruction
options.C: Permanent vision loss
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection

question: What is a major challenge that often stops clients from completing a family planning referral?

options.A: High transportation costs and distance to the receiving facility
options.B: Excessive availability of feedback slips in the primary clinic
options.C: Having too many free contraceptive options available at home
options.D: Too much emotional support provided by community health nurses

explanation: Long distances and transport money wahala are real hurdles that can discourage clients from making the trip to a secondary center.

question: What is the most immediate life-threatening complication of untreated, profuse watery diarrhea?

options.A: Hypovolemic shock from fluid loss
options.B: Enlargement of the liver and spleen
options.C: Permanent blockage of the colon
options.D: High blood pressure and stroke

explanation: Losing massive amounts of body fluid without adequate replacement drops blood volume dangerously low, leading to shock and organ failure. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: What is NOT a helpful way for a nurse manager to support research utilization on their ward?

options.A: Punishing staff members who ask questions about traditional routines
options.B: Supplying resources needed to test a new patient care procedure
options.C: Encouraging staff to try out new evidence-based bedside practices
options.D: Providing time for nurses to attend educational journal club meetings

explanation: You nailed it! Punishing curious minds kills team morale. Great managers encourage questions so everyone can grow safely.

question: Why is electrical muscle stimulation sometimes used during physical rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently replace voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: To help re-educate and stimulate muscles that have lost nerve signaling
options.C: To provide general systemic pain relief like a warm bath
options.D: To rapidly increase red blood cell production

explanation: Spot on! Gentle electrical pulses can help wake up and contract muscles that aren't receiving normal signals from the brain yet.

question: A woman has just delivered her baby ten minutes ago, and you are waiting for the placenta to separate. Which stage of labor is she currently in?

options.A: Third stage
options.B: Fourth stage
options.C: First stage
options.D: Second stage

explanation: The third stage of labor begins immediately after the baby is born and lasts until the complete delivery of the placenta. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h3)

question: What does 'U=U' (Undetectable = Untransmittable) mean for an HIV-positive person?

options.A: They are completely cured and no longer carry the virus in their body.
options.B: Their blood tests will no longer show any positive antibody results.
options.C: They cannot sexually transmit the virus if their viral load remains suppressed.
options.D: They can safely stop taking their daily medication without losing immune health.

explanation: When ART keeps the viral load undetectable, the virus cannot be passed on sexually. Amazing science!

question: Why should you sort waste right at the bedside or where it is generated?

options.A: To speed up the physical transport of bins to the incinerator
options.B: To prevent hazardous waste from contaminating general trash
options.C: To reduce the number of waste bins needed in each ward
options.D: To make it easier for patients to clean up their bedside

explanation: Sorting waste immediately stops dangerous items from mixing with safe rubbish. It keeps disposal safe and easy for everyone!

question: Which Nigerian agency works closely with the Ministry of Health to regulate and oversee drug standards?

options.A: NEMA
options.B: EFCC
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: JAMB

explanation: You know this! NAFDAC is our frontline agency in Nigeria keeping fake and unsafe drugs away from our people.

question: How can long-term social isolation negatively affect an older adult?

options.A: It stops them from developing age-related illnesses
options.B: It permanently improves their ability to stay calm
options.C: It weakens immune function and worsens mental health
options.D: It increases their daily physical endurance levels

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of connection causes chronic stress, which hurts both mental well-being and the immune system. Checking in on elderly patients matters.

question: What happens to infectious soft waste after it successfully goes through an autoclave cycle?

options.A: It becomes radioactive and needs special deep burial.
options.B: It instantly turns into liquid that pours down the drain.
options.C: It is sterilized and can often be handled like general waste.
options.D: It must still be burned in an open outdoor pit.

explanation: You're doing great! Once an autoclave kills all the infectious germs, the treated waste is safe and no longer poses a biological hazard.

question: What safety step must a nurse always take before transferring a patient into a wheelchair?

options.A: Secure the wheelchair and bed brakes
options.B: Give the patient a sedative drug
options.C: Raise the bed to the highest position
options.D: Remove all pillows from the room

explanation: Locking the wheels prevents the equipment from rolling away and causing a dangerous fall during the transfer. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h2)

question: A nurse notices that new mothers in the postnatal ward look anxious about breastfeeding. Which option turns this into a well-focused research study?

options.A: Asking every nurse on the ward how they feel about their personal jobs
options.B: Reviewing the financial cost of building a new maternity ward
options.C: Studying why the entire healthcare system in the country is failing mothers
options.D: Evaluating whether a peer support group lowers anxiety scores among first-time breastfeeding mothers

explanation: Spot on! This takes a real ward observation (breastfeeding anxiety) and turns it into a clear, measurable plan with a specific group of people.

question: What does 'personal liability' mean for you as a registered nurse?

options.A: Obligation to pay taxes on nursing salary directly to the medical board
options.B: Immunity from lawsuits if working inside a government facility
options.C: Accountability for one's own professional actions and nursing care
options.D: Financial responsibility for the entire hospital building and equipment

explanation: Personal liability means you are responsible for your own two hands. If you make a clinical error, you must answer for it individually.

question: Why does Primary Health Care place such a strong focus on community participation?

options.A: Because nurses are not trained to administer vaccines without civilian supervision
options.B: Because the government lacks any funding to pay healthcare workers
options.C: Because international laws forbid centralized hospital construction
options.D: Because programs are more successful and sustainable when locals help plan them

explanation: Exactly! When the community is involved from the start, health projects address real local needs and are warmly accepted.

question: Which question type is best for encouraging a patient to tell their story in their own words?

options.A: Closed-ended questions
options.B: Multiple-choice questions
options.C: Leading questions
options.D: Open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions allow patients to elaborate freely without limiting their responses to a single word. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why should nurses separate the concepts of 'sex' and 'gender'?

options.A: It removes the need to collect demographic data during patient admission
options.B: It ensures that patients are only treated based on their chromosome count
options.C: It helps identify which health issues stem from biology versus societal rules
options.D: It proves that biological traits change more quickly than cultural norms

explanation: Separating them helps you see the whole picture. Some health problems happen because of our biology, while others happen because of society's rules and expectations for men and women.

question: Which of these is an example of secondary data during a community assessment?

options.A: Focus group discussions with village youths
options.B: Interviews conducted with mothers at the market
options.C: Existing clinic registers and census reports
options.D: Direct observation of village water sources

explanation: Correct! Secondary data is information that's already gathered and sitting there waiting for you, like old hospital records and government census books.

question: Why should nurses be ready to talk about body image and sexual health with GU cancer patients?

options.A: Surgeries and treatments in this area directly affect elimination and sexual health
options.B: Talking about these topics completely eliminates the need for pain medication
options.C: Incontinence and sexual changes only occur in elderly female clients
options.D: Psychological support speeds up the physical regeneration of kidney tissue

explanation: Treatments for these cancers touch some of the most personal parts of a patient's life. Being a compassionate, open listener helps them cope with changes in how their body works.

question: What is the biggest danger of pouring leftover chemicals into empty beverage bottles?

options.A: The chemical instantly turns into a harmless gas
options.B: Labels become permanently stamped into the plastic
options.C: People may accidentally drink the toxic chemical
options.D: The plastic material dissolves within a few hours

explanation: You got it! Putting chemicals in drink bottles is a recipe for disaster because it tricks anyone—especially thirsty children—into thinking it's safe juice or water.

question: Why is it important to document what the lesion or discharge looks like after swabbing?

options.A: To provide a clear baseline for tracking clinical progress
options.B: To prove to the laboratory technician that a swab was necessary
options.C: To satisfy insurance requirements for billing the laboratory test
options.D: To ensure the patient remembers how the symptoms appeared

explanation: Writing a clear description gives the healthcare team a baseline so they can easily check if the treatment is working during the next visit.

question: During which step of mobilisation do community members and nurses figure out what resources and tasks are needed?

options.A: Immediate closure
options.B: Final evaluation
options.C: Strict policing
options.D: Action planning

explanation: Action planning is where the community maps out tasks, responsibilities, and timelines using local resources. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h5)

question: What do we call the tight, stiff, and involuntary muscle tone that often happens after a brain injury?

options.A: Contracture
options.B: Spasticity
options.C: Flaccidity
options.D: Atrophy

explanation: Spasticity is when muscles stay constantly contracted and stiff, making it tricky for the client to move or relax their limbs smoothly.

question: What is the primary goal of community mobilisation?

options.A: Enforcing strict national health laws in rural villages
options.B: Replacing traditional healers with modern medical doctors
options.C: Collecting financial taxes for local health clinics
options.D: Empowering community members to solve local problems together

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on bringing people together so they can take charge of their own health issues and find local solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h1)

question: A patient has colon cancer, and a scan shows the cancer has now traveled to the liver. What is this secondary growth called?

options.A: Metastasis
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Encapsulation
options.D: Angiogenesis

explanation: When cancer cells pack their bags and travel from their original home to a brand new organ, we call it metastasis.

question: You are getting ready to change a surgical wound dressing on a patient's kitchen table. What action shows proper technique?

options.A: Spraying the entire wooden kitchen table with surgical disinfectant
options.B: Placing a clean waterproof barrier underneath the sterile supplies
options.C: Performing the procedure without gloves since it is a home setting
options.D: Asking the family to clear all furniture out of the room completely

explanation: Brilliant! Laying down a clean waterproof barrier creates a safe zone for your sterile equipment, protecting it from ordinary household tables. You're thinking like a pro!

question: Why do we put healthy-feeling people into quarantine after a known exposure to a contagious illness?

options.A: To monitor them through the incubation period before they can spread the disease asymptomatically
options.B: To punish individuals who failed to maintain proper personal hygiene standards
options.C: To immediately administer therapeutic antibiotics regardless of the actual pathogen involved
options.D: To provide them with active immunity through immediate vaccination in a controlled facility

explanation: Spot on! It catches sneaky infections early so they don't pass them on to others before showing symptoms.

question: How does doing night shifts and changing schedules over and over affect a theatre nurse?

options.A: It makes your relationship with doctors and colleagues stronger
options.B: It messes up your sleep, leaving you tired and less alert
options.C: It completely stops any muscle or joint aches
options.D: It balances out your body clock and boosts immunity

explanation: Constantly switching your sleep routine fights against your body's natural clock, making you extra tired and more prone to mistakes. Rest when you can!

question: What is the main goal of organizing a nursing unit?

options.A: Eliminating the need for nursing documentation
options.B: Reducing the overall number of patients admitted
options.C: Arranging staff and resources for safe patient care
options.D: Lowering the monthly salary costs for the hospital

explanation: Great job! Unit organization is all about setting up people and materials so that care flows smoothly and safely. Keep it up!

question: In a female body, which organs make up the 'gonads' part of the HPG axis?

options.A: The mammary glands
options.B: The fallopian tubes
options.C: The uterus
options.D: The ovaries

explanation: Spot on! Gonads are the primary reproductive organs—testes in males and ovaries in females.

question: Who is primarily responsible for keeping track of surgical instruments and sponges in the operating room?

options.A: The anaesthetist and the operating room manager
options.B: The lead surgeon and the assistant surgeon
options.C: The circulator nurse and the scrub nurse
options.D: The central sterile supply department technician

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! The scrub nurse and circulator nurse double-team the counts to make sure nothing is left behind.

question: How do most medications pass from a nursing mother's blood into her breast milk?

options.A: Cellular phagocytosis
options.B: Active transport pumps
options.C: Passive diffusion
options.D: Direct ductal injection

explanation: Just like with the placenta, drugs usually drift naturally across membranes into breast milk based on concentration and fat solubility.

question: Which lab result is a classic sign right after a patient suffers a major burn and goes into shock?

options.A: Decreased serum potassium levels
options.B: Decreased white blood cell count
options.C: Elevated platelet count from bone marrow failure
options.D: Elevated hematocrit due to fluid loss

explanation: Since the liquid part of the blood (plasma) leaks out into the body, what's left behind is thick blood! This makes the hematocrit shoot up until IV fluids balance things out.

question: Why must nurses in Nigeria ask patients about traditional herbs or local concoctions during a drug history check?

options.A: Local herbs replace the need for checking kidney function tests.
options.B: Traditional mixtures are always completely harmless and speed up healing.
options.C: Herbs can interact with prescription drugs and cause unexpected adverse reactions.
options.D: Hospitals require herbal documentation to qualify for government funding.

explanation: Patients often use local herbs alongside hospital medications. Knowing about them helps us catch and prevent dangerous drug-herb clashes!

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of a community health nurse in immunization programs?

options.A: Educating mothers on the schedule of routine immunizations
options.B: Tracking children who default on their vaccination doses
options.C: Manufacturing synthetic vaccine formulas in the local clinic
options.D: Administering vaccines safely while maintaining cold chain

explanation: Nurses administer, educate, and track patients, but vaccine manufacturing happens in specialized pharmaceutical laboratories, not local clinics. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is birth spacing emphasized during family planning counseling for postpartum women?

options.A: It allows the mother's body and nutrient stores to recover fully
options.B: It prevents the mother from ever experiencing menopause
options.C: It guarantees that all future children will be born male
options.D: It eliminates the need for any future medical checkups

explanation: Spacing pregnancies gives the mother adequate time to restore her health and nutritional reserves, leading to better outcomes for subsequent children. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h6)

question: How can nurses help solve scheduling problems caused by traditional family and caregiving duties?

options.A: By offering clinic hours that accommodate domestic responsibilities
options.B: By charging extra fees for patients who arrive late
options.C: By refusing to treat patients who have caregiving duties
options.D: By keeping clinics open only during standard morning work hours

explanation: Flexible clinic timings make it possible for people juggling heavy caregiving duties to still get the medical care they need. Wonderful thinking!

question: How often should a bedbound patient ideally be repositioned to prevent pressure injuries?

options.A: Only when the patient complains
options.B: Once every twelve hours
options.C: At least every two hours
options.D: Once per day during the morning shift

explanation: Turning or repositioning a patient every two hours relieves continuous pressure on vulnerable skin areas and tissues. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of mechanical digestion?

options.A: To change proteins directly into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid before food enters the bowel
options.C: To transport nutrients through the intestinal wall
options.D: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes

explanation: Mechanical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces, which gives digestive enzymes more surface area to work on. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of disrupted ovarian cycles?

options.A: Severe physical or emotional stress
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Extreme weight loss or eating disorders
options.D: Drinking adequate daily water

explanation: Normal fluid intake supports health but does not disrupt the delicate hormonal axis that controls ovulation, unlike severe stress, weight loss, or disease states. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h7)

question: Who do PTAs often collaborate with to run school immunization and deworming programs?

options.A: Community health nurses
options.B: Federal road safety officers
options.C: Building contractors
options.D: Commercial bank managers

explanation: Community health nurses are the primary healthcare professionals who partner with schools for immunization and routine checks. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h5)

question: How can tiny genetic differences in liver enzymes cause an idiosyncratic reaction?

options.A: They create harmful chemical byproducts that damage healthy body cells.
options.B: They force the kidneys to produce too much urine and dehydrate the patient.
options.C: They stop the drug from dissolving in the stomach completely.
options.D: They cause the body to eliminate the medicine before it can enter the blood.

explanation: Sometimes, a patient's liver enzymes process a drug a bit differently, accidentally turning it into a toxic byproduct that irritates or damages healthy cells.

question: What usually happens if a patient's thinking part of the brain is badly damaged, but their brainstem is totally fine?

options.A: The patient loses awareness of the environment but may still sleep and wake
options.B: The patient loses all reflex actions while keeping clear thoughts
options.C: The patient stays completely awake but loses the ability to feel pain
options.D: The patient enters an immediate state of permanent brain death

explanation: You're doing great! Because the brainstem handles sleep-wake cycles, an undamaged brainstem means the body can still cycle between sleeping and waking up, even without higher thinking.

question: How should you respond when a client uses unhealthy coping tricks like total denial or locking themselves away from others?

options.A: Immediately discharge the client from home care services
options.B: Ignore the behavior because it will naturally resolve itself
options.C: Confront the behaviors with empathy rather than harsh judgment
options.D: Scold the client for failing to follow the rehabilitation plan

explanation: Harshness pushes people further into their shell. Meeting them with patience and understanding gives them a safe space to start healing emotionally.

question: Why is early ambulation strongly encouraged after pelvic surgeries like a hysterectomy?

options.A: It prevents venous stasis and reduces the risk of blood clots
options.B: It forces the surgical incision to heal much faster
options.C: It restores immediate hormonal balance in the body
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for postoperative pain relief

explanation: Getting patients moving early promotes lower extremity circulation, significantly lowering the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h6)

question: What score do you give when a patient correctly follows simple commands, like squeezing your hand when asked?
explanation: Obeying commands is the highest motor score possible—a solid 6! It's always a relief to see a patient do this.

question: What is meant by the 'utilization rate' of a healthcare facility?

options.A: How quickly the pharmacy dispenses routine medications
options.B: The total number of chairs in the hospital waiting room
options.C: The monthly electricity bill paid by the clinic
options.D: How often community members actually visit and use the services

explanation: Utilization rate measures the extent to which the target population uses available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why should you as a nurse always ask your patients if they use traditional herbs or local remedies?

options.A: To report illegal practitioners to the local authorities
options.B: To calculate the exact economic cost of local healthcare
options.C: To prevent dangerous interactions with hospital medications
options.D: To replace all expensive hospital drugs with free herbs

explanation: Patients often mix local herbs with hospital drugs without mentioning it. Checking for this helps keep them safe from unexpected drug reactions. You're learning to think like a safe, caring nurse!

question: What is the main job of the fluid made by the seminal vesicles?

options.A: Storing mature sperm cells
options.B: Nourishing sperm with fructose
options.C: Lubricating the urethra
options.D: Neutralizing acidic urine

explanation: You've got this! Seminal vesicle fluid is packed with fructose, giving sperm the energy boost they need to swim toward the egg.

question: What is the main job of the urethral sphincter in normal bladder control?

options.A: To sense when the bladder is completely full
options.B: To push urine out of the bladder during voiding
options.C: To stay contracted and maintain a tight seal against urine leakage
options.D: To stretch when the bladder fills with urine

explanation: The urethral sphincter acts like a tight valve, staying closed to keep urine inside until you're ready to use the bathroom.

question: A nurse cleans a child's thigh for a vaccine, but then touches the exact spot with a bare finger to check the muscle landmark. What is the correct action?

options.A: Proceed with the injection since the finger was recently washed
options.B: Wipe the skin with a dry cotton ball and give the vaccine
options.C: Change the needle on the syringe and inject immediately
options.D: Clean the skin again with a new alcohol swab and let it dry

explanation: Touching the cleansed skin with a bare finger contaminates the site, requiring the nurse to repeat the skin cleaning step before proceeding. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h4)

question: When should you seal and replace a sharps disposal box?

options.A: When it is completely filled to the absolute brim
options.B: Whenever the outer cardboard gets slightly dusty
options.C: When it is three-quarters full
options.D: At the end of every single calendar month

explanation: Stop at the three-quarter mark! Waiting until it's overflowing invites accidental needle pricks.

question: How did the industrial revolution change the way people approached community health?

options.A: It forced governments to address crowded living conditions and sanitation
options.B: It eliminated all chronic illnesses through factory safety regulations
options.C: It shifted nursing care exclusively into high-tech urban intensive care units
options.D: It removed the need for community health nurses by eradicating poverty

explanation: Think about fast-growing cities during industrial times—crowded conditions created massive health issues that meant public health had to step up!

question: How do regular performance appraisals help integrate personal and organisational goals?

options.A: By replacing the need for clinical nursing documentation
options.B: By ensuring that no nurse ever receives a promotion
options.C: By providing a platform for supervisors and nurses to discuss mutual expectations
options.D: By giving management an excuse to cut nurse salaries every month

explanation: Appraisals shouldn't feel like a witch hunt. They are a great chance to sit down, talk about your career growth, and line it up with the hospital's goals.

question: What was the main drive behind early caregiving in ancient and medieval times?

options.A: Securing high financial profit
options.B: Religious duty and humanitarian support
options.C: Earning formal university degrees
options.D: Meeting government licensing requirements

explanation: Great job! Long before professional licenses and paychecks, early caregivers were driven by faith and a deep moral duty to help the vulnerable.

question: Why is eating a balanced diet important when managing chronic fatigue?

options.A: It stops the digestive system from producing inflammatory enzymes.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any physical rest during the day.
options.C: It prevents blood sugar swings that drain daily energy reserves.
options.D: It directly increases the number of red blood cells in the liver.

explanation: Exactly! Balanced meals keep blood sugar stable. Big sugar spikes and crashes only make fatigue worse, so steady food equals steady energy.

question: Which major complication do rehabilitation nurses constantly work to prevent?

options.A: Sudden visual impairment
options.B: Spontaneous bone fractures
options.C: Acute myocardial infarction
options.D: Pressure injuries and contractures

explanation: Great job! Because rehab patients often spend a lot of time resting, nurses watch closely to prevent bed sores (pressure injuries) and stiff joints (contractures).

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended for women after childbirth?

options.A: To strengthen muscles and prevent urinary incontinence
options.B: To increase the total volume of breastmilk produced
options.C: To help tighten abdominal skin after a C-section
options.D: To accelerate the growth of the newborn's bones

explanation: Spot on! Pregnancy and pushing during birth stretch out the pelvic floor. Doing these targeted exercises helps tone those muscles back up and stops bladder leakage issues.

question: Which newborn scalp swelling is known for crossing right across the cranial suture lines?

options.A: Subgaleal hemorrhage
options.B: Cephalhematoma
options.C: Caput succedaneum
options.D: Subdural hematoma

explanation: Correct! Caput is just fluid under the scalp skin, so it easily crosses over the suture lines. Think of it like a soft, spongy cushion.

question: A community health nurse wants to help reduce FGM rates in a rural village. Which strategy works best for lasting change?

options.A: Ignoring the practice to avoid offending cultural traditions
options.B: Performing mild pricks in the clinic to keep traditions alive safely
options.C: Engaging local leaders and educators in discussions about health risks
options.D: Arresting every mother without talking to the community

explanation: Brilliant! Real, lasting change happens when you work hand-in-hand with the community to shift mindsets and choose health together.

question: Why do qualitative researchers keep a reflexive journal throughout their study?

options.A: To monitor and reflect on their own personal biases
options.B: To write personal diary entries about their coworkers
options.C: To record daily weather patterns in the hospital ward
options.D: To keep track of how much money they spent on printing

explanation: You nailed it! Reflexivity helps us check our own personal opinions and background so we don't accidentally twist what our patients are telling us.

question: What is a major benefit of involving local community leaders in reproductive health programs?

options.A: It allows community members to perform complex surgical operations
options.B: It builds local ownership and encourages people to use health services early
options.C: It eliminates the requirement for government funding in hospitals
options.D: It removes the need for trained nurses in rural health posts

explanation: When community leaders are involved, people trust the program more, drop harmful myths, and come to the clinic early for help. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h8)

question: Which emotional response is a patient most likely to show after being told they have permanent vision loss?

options.A: Grief and frustration as they adjust to the change
options.B: Total indifference with no emotional reaction at all
options.C: Immediate excitement to learn new computer skills
options.D: Excessive hunger and sudden weight gain

explanation: Losing one's sight is a major life-changing event. It is completely normal for patients to feel grief, frustration, and sadness as they process the news.

question: Why does community health nursing go beyond just giving care at the bedside?

options.A: To reduce the number of trained doctors needed in clinics
options.B: To replace traditional hospital treatments entirely
options.C: To address environmental and social factors affecting health
options.D: To focus exclusively on rare surgical complications

explanation: Spot on! Things like housing, clean water, and daily living conditions shape a population's health just as much as medicine does.

question: Why is heavy reliance on out-of-pocket payments a major problem for patients?

options.A: It forces sick families to pay directly at the point of care, often causing poverty
options.B: It prevents the government from collecting taxes
options.C: It makes doctors prescribe too many laboratory tests
options.D: It forces hospitals to close down their administrative offices

explanation: Paying cash directly for every service at the hospital door ruins household finances during emergencies. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is an important step before putting a fresh layer of ointment on a patient's skin?

options.A: Apply a drying alcohol swab over the entire lesion
options.B: Scrub the area vigorously with an antiseptic brush
options.C: Warm the skin using a high-heat therapeutic lamp
options.D: Gently cleanse the skin to remove old medication

explanation: Always wash away old residue gently! This prevents buildup, stops irritation, and lets the fresh medicine do its job properly.

question: Which brain structure acts as the main relay station for incoming sensory messages before they reach the cortex?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Thalamus
options.D: Pons

explanation: Spot on! The thalamus is like a busy airport control tower, sorting and routing almost all incoming sensory signals to the correct spots in the brain.

question: Why is using a gait belt so helpful when assisting a patient to stand and walk?

options.A: It corrects the patient's posture automatically without active effort
options.B: It gives the nurse a secure grip to prevent falls if the patient loses balance
options.C: It completely stops the patient from feeling dizzy while standing up
options.D: It replaces the need for a physical therapist during early walking sessions

explanation: A gait belt gives you a safe handle around the patient's waist, making it much easier to catch them safely if their legs wobble.

question: Why does the egg trigger the cortical reaction right after a sperm gets inside?

options.A: To block entry by additional sperm cells
options.B: To double the size of the egg cell
options.C: To trigger the first mitotic division
options.D: To stimulate the release of progesterone

explanation: Spot on! The egg quickly puts up a chemical shield so no extra sperm can enter, ensuring the right amount of genetic material.

question: If a lab report describes a bacteria as a 'bacillus', what shape does it have?

options.A: Spherical clusters
options.B: Rod-shaped
options.C: Spiral corkscrews
options.D: Comma-shaped loops

explanation: Bacilli are shaped like little rods or cylinders. (Spherical ones are cocci, and spirals are spirilla—you'll nail these terms in no time!)

question: Which of these belongs inside the methodology section?

options.A: Detailed graphs showing the final statistical outcomes
options.B: A comprehensive list of every textbook found in the library

options.C: Conventional foods contain prescription drugs that supplements completely lack

explanation: Real foods give you a rich mix of fiber and interacting nutrients that a single pill just can't copy. Balance is key!

question: What can happen during rectal insertion if you forget to use a lubricant?

options.A: Complete liver enzyme shutdown
options.B: Sudden systemic hypertension
options.C: Mucosal tearing and irritation
options.D: Rapid dehydration of the skin

explanation: Without lubricant, the friction can easily scrape and injure the delicate rectal lining.

question: What is the main goal of routine GI screenings like a colonoscopy?

options.A: To cure existing advanced infections instantly without medicine
options.B: To detect polyps and early-stage cancer before symptoms start
options.C: To measure the exact daily caloric intake of the patient
options.D: To replace the need for healthy eating and hydration

explanation: Screening lets doctors catch tiny growths or early changes long before they turn into major problems.

question: Which part of Nigeria generally records lower modern contraceptive prevalence rates?

options.A: Major coastal ports
options.B: Capital city districts
options.C: The Southern zones
options.D: The Northern zones

explanation: National health surveys consistently show differences in mCPR across regions, with the northern zones generally recording lower rates than the southern zones.

question: What is the biggest health benefit of colostrum (the first breastmilk)?

options.A: It supplies excess fat calories to promote rapid weight gain
options.B: It provides high concentrations of protective antibodies and protein
options.C: It contains high levels of iron to prevent infant anemia
options.D: It acts as a strong laxative to prevent infantile jaundice

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold for the baby! It's packed with antibodies that coat their tummy and protect their brand-new immune system against germs.

question: A nurse evaluates a disaster program and notices residents still cannot point out their local evacuation route. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Remove all warning signs to encourage independent learning
options.B: Report the community residents to local law enforcement
options.C: Assume the community is fully prepared and stop teaching
options.D: Change up the teaching style and provide follow-up education

explanation: You nailed it! Finding a learning gap just means it's time to try a new teaching approach so the community feels confident and prepared.

question: What is the main difference between a medical emergency and a surgical emergency?

options.A: Surgical emergencies never involve internal bleeding
options.B: Medical emergencies always require immediate surgery
options.C: Medical emergencies only happen outside the hospital
options.D: Surgical emergencies usually require an operation to fix

explanation: You've got this! Surgical emergencies involve physical trauma or acute organ trouble that typically needs an operation to fix, while medical emergencies usually stem from internal illnesses. Think surgery vs. medicine!

question: How can NSAIDs cause trouble for a patient's kidneys?

options.A: By forcing the kidneys to excrete too much potassium
options.B: By directly destroying kidney nephrons with toxic chemical crystals
options.C: By causing the bladder to spasm and block urine output
options.D: By reducing blood flow to the kidneys through prostaglandin inhibition

explanation: Prostaglandins act like traffic controllers keeping renal blood vessels nice and open. Block them, and the blood supply to the kidneys drops. Good to watch out for in dehydrated patients! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of filing an incident report after a medication mistake?

options.A: To collect financial fines from the pharmacy department
options.B: To provide gossip material for the nursing station
options.C: To identify system flaws and prevent future mistakes
options.D: To ensure the responsible nurse gets fired immediately

explanation: Incident reports aren't about blame—they help the team figure out what went wrong in the workflow so we can fix it and protect future patients.

question: What often causes the biggest hurdles for people with physical disabilities in daily life?

options.A: Inaccessible physical environments and negative social attitudes
options.B: A lack of interest in attending family social gatherings
options.C: The mandatory use of modern assistive walking frames
options.D: Excessive consumption of prescribed rehabilitation vitamins

explanation: Often, bad societal attitudes and buildings without ramps or lifts cause more barriers than the physical condition itself. We must be change agents!

question: What pregnancy hormone is most closely linked to the timing of first-trimester nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.C: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.D: Luteinizing hormone

explanation: Human chorionic gonadotropin peaks during the first trimester right when nausea and vomiting are usually at their worst. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h1)

question: A healthy pregnant woman at 26 weeks gestation goes for her routine antenatal clinic. Why is a glucose screening typically included?

options.A: To check for gestational diabetes that can develop during pregnancy
options.B: To confirm the exact gestational age of the growing fetus
options.C: To test her kidney function against pregnancy hormones
options.D: To measure how much iron she is storing in her liver

explanation: Pregnancy hormones can cause insulin resistance, making routine screening for gestational diabetes essential during the second trimester. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: A bacterium
options.B: A protozoan
options.C: A fungus
options.D: A prion

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, single-celled parasite (a protozoan) that loves to cause irritation and unusual discharge.

question: What does gender-based violence (GBV) mean in simple terms?

options.A: Any harmful act directed against someone based on their gender
options.B: Accidental injuries sustained during high-contact sports
options.C: Physical fights that happen exclusively between married couples
options.D: Violent crimes committed only against adult males in public spaces

explanation: You've got this! GBV is any harmful act forced on someone simply because of their gender. It stems from unequal power and societal expectations. Keep up the great work!

question: What is the texture of a pureed diet?

options.A: Small, bite-sized pieces of tender meat
options.B: A smooth, pudding-like paste with no lumps
options.C: A mixture of solid chunks and thin liquids
options.D: Crispy foods that dissolve easily in the mouth

explanation: Pureed diets require zero chewing because all foods are blended completely smooth. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h3)

question: What is the standard prescription cream applied from the neck down to treat scabies?

options.A: Hydrocortisone 1% ointment
options.B: Permethrin 5% cream
options.C: Clotrimazole antifungal lotion
options.D: Zinc oxide barrier paste

explanation: Permethrin 5% is our go-to weapon. Applied properly from the neck down, it safely wipes out both the mites and their eggs.

question: Which of the following is a simple, effective home method to make unsafe drinking water safer?

options.A: Adding heavy machine oil to the bucket
options.B: Boiling the water thoroughly
options.C: Leaving the water uncovered in the sun
options.D: Stirring the water with a dirty stick

explanation: Boiling kills harmful bacteria, viruses, and parasites present in untreated water sources. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is dyspareunia, a common complaint among FGM survivors?

options.A: Severe fear of hospital environments
options.B: Chronic swelling of the lower legs
options.C: Inability to produce breast milk
options.D: Painful sexual intercourse

explanation: Dyspareunia simply means persistent pain during sex, usually resulting from severe scarring and nerve damage. Knowing this helps you support your patients better!

question: When should you avoid doing passive range of motion exercises on a limb?

options.A: When the client has a fresh, unhealed bone fracture
options.B: When the ward weather is unusually warm
options.C: When the client has a mild cold
options.D: When the client feels sleepy in the afternoon

explanation: Spot on! Moving a limb with a fresh fracture disrupts bone healing and causes severe pain. Always check for fractures first!

question: A researcher wants to study nurses in Abuja and gets the official staff register from the ministry. What is this register called?

options.A: The final sample
options.B: The inclusion criteria
options.C: The sampling frame
options.D: The target population

explanation: Spot on! That staff register serves as the concrete list you draw your participants from, making it your sampling frame.

question: What are the three main categories in the biopsychosocial model?

options.A: Genetics, environment, and medication
options.B: Biological, psychological, and social factors
options.C: Emotional, behavioral, and cultural traits
options.D: Physical, spiritual, and financial factors

explanation: The biopsychosocial model organizes the causes of mental illness into three core dimensions: biological, psychological, and social. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h1)

question: When checking for urinary retention, what does a nurse feel for in the lower belly?

options.A: A firm, rounded bladder above the pubic bone
options.B: Soft, empty folds of skin near the belly button
options.C: Warm fluid moving freely inside the intestines
options.D: A hard, pulsing mass on the left side

explanation: When urine gets trapped (retention), the bladder fills up and feels like a firm dome right above the pubic bone.

question: Which of these checks is NOT needed before using a sterile instrument pack?

options.A: Confirming that the sterilization expiration date has not passed
options.B: Verifying that the equipment inside has been polished to a shine
options.C: Inspecting the outer package for rips, tears, or punctures
options.D: Checking that the chemical indicator strip changed color properly

explanation: Shiny instruments look nice, but patient safety is all about checking for tears, expiration dates, and color changes on the indicator!

question: When is a patient usually considered for epilepsy surgery?

options.A: Only when the patient refuses to take any pills at all
options.B: Immediately upon receiving the first diagnosis of a seizure
options.C: When seizures persist despite trying multiple appropriate medications
options.D: When the electroencephalogram shows a normal brain pattern

explanation: Surgery is saved for drug-resistant cases where standard medications have been tried properly but still haven't stopped the seizures. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h6)

question: What tragic emotional outcome is sometimes seen among young brides who feel completely trapped with no way out?

options.A: Bipolar manic episodes
options.B: Suicide and self-harm
options.C: Dissociative identity disorder
options.D: Pathological compulsive gambling

explanation: That's correct. Overwhelming hopelessness and a lack of support drive some desperate young brides to self-harm or suicide.

question: What is the main job of vitamin D made in the skin?

options.A: Preventing ultraviolet radiation damage to cells
options.B: Eliminating excess urea through sweat glands
options.C: Assisting with calcium absorption in the body
options.D: Regulating core body temperature during a fever

explanation: Great job! Sunlight on the skin helps create vitamin D, which your body needs to properly absorb calcium for strong bones and teeth.

question: Which of these is a major red flag that supervisors look out for during a data audit?

options.A: Reporting zero waste while consumption numbers are very high
options.B: Having more than two nurses sign the document
options.C: Submitting the monthly report on the exact final day
options.D: Using blue ink instead of black ink on the monitoring form

explanation: Spot on! In a busy clinic, zero waste is almost impossible. It usually means the numbers were guessed or made up.

question: Which health problem is a well-known long-term risk for patients taking steroids for a long time?

options.A: Chronic hypotension
options.B: Enhanced night vision
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Rapid weight loss

explanation: Long-term steroid use makes it harder for the body to absorb calcium and build strong bone, putting patients at higher risk for weak bones (osteoporosis).

question: Why is the incubation period tricky for community health, even when the person feels totally fine?

options.A: Pathogens multiply faster when the host feels healthy
options.B: Lab tests cannot detect any trace of the pathogen
options.C: The person can unknowingly spread the pathogen to others
options.D: The immune system is permanently damaged during this time

explanation: Exactly! Because they feel healthy and show no signs of illness, they go about their normal day and can pass the bug to others without knowing it.

question: What happens when food moves way too quickly through a person's colon?

options.A: Ulceration
options.B: Appendicitis
options.C: Diarrhea
options.D: Constipation

explanation: If food rushes through the colon, there's no time to absorb water, leading to loose, watery stools. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: How are Type IV hypersensitivity reactions different from Types I, II, and III?

options.A: They only happen inside internal organs, never on the skin
options.B: They are driven by T-cells and take days to develop instead of using fast antibodies
options.C: They destroy red blood cells using complement proteins
options.D: They are only triggered by eating certain foods

explanation: Unlike the other types that rely on quick antibodies, Type IV is a 'delayed' reaction. It relies on T-lymphocytes taking a few days to show up and cause a reaction (like a bad rash).

question: What is the main job of glial cells in the nervous system?

options.A: To connect bone to bone across movable joints
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.C: To support, protect, and nourish the neurons
options.D: To form a tough protective membrane around the brain

explanation: Think of glial cells as the supportive backup team—they take care of the neurons so the neurons can focus on sending signals!

question: Why is proper lighting and full exposure of the joint necessary during a musculoskeletal assessment?

options.A: To make it easier for the doctor to read the laboratory results
options.B: To prevent the patient from feeling cold in the examination room
options.C: To ensure the patient's blood pressure remains stable throughout the test
options.D: To accurately observe subtle skin changes, swelling, and muscle symmetry

explanation: Good light and clear visibility let the nurse spot minor differences in size, shape, or color between limbs. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main reason we give intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) for malaria during pregnancy?

options.A: To boost the mother's daily caloric and protein intake
options.B: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes mellitus
options.C: To cure a chronic respiratory infection in the mother
options.D: To reduce placental malaria parasitemia and associated risks

explanation: In malaria-endemic areas like ours, IPTp stops malaria parasites from hiding out in the placenta where they can harm both mother and baby.

question: What is the primary goal of Adolescent and Youth-Friendly Health Services?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on the treatment of geriatric illnesses
options.B: Banning teenagers from visiting local community pharmacies
options.C: Providing confidential and accessible care without judgment
options.D: Requiring parental consent for every routine consultation

explanation: That's right! Youth-friendly centers remove barriers like judgmental attitudes and lack of privacy so young people feel safe seeking help.

question: Why is cultural humility crucial for a community health nurse?

options.A: It helps the nurse respect local beliefs and build trust with community members
options.B: It prevents the nurse from ever needing to wash their hands
options.C: It ensures the nurse receives a higher salary from the government
options.D: It allows the nurse to diagnose complex surgical conditions instantly

explanation: Understanding and respecting local traditions breaks down barriers and encourages people to accept health advice and services. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h8)

question: A patient with severe malaria isn't getting better despite finishing a full course of drugs bought from an unverified roadside vendor. What should you suspect?

options.A: The patient requires an immediate surgical intervention for appendicitis.
options.B: The hospital ward is experiencing an outbreak of a normal bacterial infection.
options.C: The patient's body has suddenly developed a lifelong immunity to all fevers.
options.D: The medication administered may be substandard or counterfeit.

explanation: When a trusted drug completely fails to work—especially from a shady source—always suspect that it might be a fake or low-quality product.

question: Why are unannounced kitchen inspections usually better than scheduled visits?

options.A: They ensure that all food items are cooked at very high heat
options.B: They give the kitchen staff time to hide dirty equipment
options.C: They reduce the amount of paperwork the supervisor must complete
options.D: They show normal, everyday kitchen habits and practices

explanation: Surprise checks mean staff can't just clean up and put on a show temporarily for the inspector. Makes total sense!

question: What is the first step when a patient's airway is blocked by secretions in a community clinic?

options.A: Applying high-pressure chest compressions
options.B: Starting an immediate intravenous infusion of normal saline
options.C: Clearing the airway using proper positioning and suctioning
options.D: Administering sublingual nitroglycerin tablets

explanation: Airway comes first in every emergency! Positioning the patient and clearing out any blockage gets them breathing easier.

question: What is a major cause of clinical errors when patients are being transferred between care teams?

options.A: Excessive time spent resting on duty
options.B: Overuse of basic patient hygiene supplies
options.C: Strict adherence to written safety checklists
options.D: Communication breakdowns during handovers

explanation: Spot on! Poor communication during shift changes or patient transfers often leads to missed details, making handovers a high-risk moment for mistakes.

question: Which of the following is classified as pathological waste?

options.A: Used paper hand towels
options.B: Broken mercury thermometers
options.C: Surgically removed human tissues
options.D: Expired paracetamol tablets

explanation: Pathological waste specifically includes human tissues, organs, and body parts removed during surgeries or autopsies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication that can significantly influence a patient interaction?

options.A: The specific medical terminology used in the care plan
options.B: Open posture and relaxed facial expressions
options.C: A printed schedule of clinic operating hours
options.D: The speed at which discharge instructions are read aloud

explanation: Body language, posture, and facial expressions are non-verbal cues that convey openness, empathy, or disinterest without using words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: A critically ill patient just received a lot of IV fluids. Which sign helps you catch early fluid overload?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on both lower legs
options.B: A slight drop in body temperature
options.C: Developing crackles in the lung bases
options.D: An increase in the patient's daily appetite

explanation: Too much fluid in the system quickly backs up into the lungs, creating those classic crackling sounds when you listen with your stethoscope.

question: Why do many pregnant women notice dark skin patches like the linea nigra on their belly?

options.A: The liver temporarily stops filtering waste pigments properly
options.B: Extra blood pools near the surface due to high progesterone
options.C: Sunlight exposure affects pregnant skin much faster than normal
options.D: Estrogen stimulates increased melanin production in the skin

explanation: Exactly! Surging estrogen wakes up the skin cells that make pigment (melanin), causing those familiar dark lines and patches during pregnancy.

question: What does decontamination do for a dirty surgical instrument right after use?

options.A: It achieves absolute sterility without the need for an autoclave machine
options.B: It removes organic soil and lowers bioburden so staff can handle the tool safely
options.C: It replaces the need for thorough high-level chemical disinfection
options.D: It permanently alters the metal alloy to prevent future corrosion in storage

explanation: Decontamination is your first line of defense. It washes away heavy dirt so you can handle the tools without risking an infection.

question: What is the main job of the mucus layer inside your gut?

options.A: To produce digestive enzymes that break down dietary fats
options.B: To absorb complex carbohydrates straight into your bloodstream
options.C: To speed up how fast waste moves through the colon
options.D: To trap bicarbonate and protect your stomach cells from harsh acid

explanation: Think of mucus as a protective shield! It holds bicarbonate right against your stomach lining to neutralize strong digestive acids so they don't harm your cells.

question: What is a double-barreled question in a research instrument?

options.A: A question that has more than ten possible answers
options.B: A question written in two different languages
options.C: A question that is asked twice during an interview
options.D: A question that asks about two different things at once

explanation: Double-barreled questions confuse respondents because they combine multiple ideas into a single query. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h4)

question: Which medication group forms the first step of the WHO analgesic ladder?

options.A: Strong agonists like fentanyl
options.B: Pure antagonists like naloxone
options.C: Intravenous muscle relaxants
options.D: Non-opioids like paracetamol

explanation: For mild pain, we always start simple at Step One with basic non-opioids like paracetamol or ibuprofen, plus an adjuvant if needed.

question: What is the primary role of the cerebellum in the nervous system?

options.A: Coordinating smooth muscle movement and balance
options.B: Processing conscious thoughts and logical reasoning
options.C: Regulating basic body temperature and hunger
options.D: Relaying pain signals from the skin to the brain

explanation: The cerebellum ensures that physical movements are smooth, balanced, and properly timed. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h5)

question: A nurse wants to help secondary school girls prevent anemia using local foods. Which tip is the most practical?

options.A: Drink lots of black tea right after every big meal
options.B: Eat sugary snacks between classes for quick energy
options.C: Eat local dark greens, beans, and vitamin C-rich fruits
options.D: Avoid all animal protein and fish products

explanation: Spot on! Local greens and beans give iron, and adding vitamin C (like a squeeze of orange or lemon) helps the body absorb that iron much better!

question: Why is the nurse considered a vital link in community reproductive health?

options.A: Nurses perform all surgical procedures related to reproductive organs
options.B: Nurses have the sole authority to distribute contraceptive drugs
options.C: Nurses connect community members to formal health institutions and provide primary care
options.D: Nurses write the national policies governing family planning services

explanation: Nurses work directly within communities and clinics, making them the primary bridge for education, prevention, and basic care delivery. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why must a nurse use a non-stretchable tape when measuring head and arm circumferences?

options.A: To prevent measurement errors caused by material stretching over time
options.B: To ensure the tape can be washed easily with boiling water
options.C: To comply with weight limits on heavy clinical scales
options.D: To make the equipment safe for the child to play with

explanation: Materials stretch with use! If your tape stretches, your next readings will be off, messing up the child's growth tracking records.

question: A patient has worried endlessly about money for over a year and now feels constantly exhausted and sick. Which GAS stage is this?

options.A: Alarm stage
options.B: Recovery stage
options.C: Resistance stage
options.D: Exhaustion stage

explanation: When stress drags on too long, the body runs completely out of coping reserves. That's the exhaustion stage where immunity drops.

question: Why do children under five suffer the highest morbidity and mortality rates from malaria and diarrhea in many developing regions?

options.A: Children consume more medication than adults, leading to toxic reactions
options.B: Their immune systems are still developing and they face environmental vulnerabilities
options.C: Medical researchers focus exclusively on adult diseases instead
options.D: They are more likely to refuse treatment given by community health workers

explanation: Young children have immature immunity and often live in environments with limited access to clean water and prompt malaria treatment. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which questionnaire is widely used to check different parts of female sexual function?

options.A: Mini-Mental State Examination
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Beck Depression Inventory
options.D: Female Sexual Function Index

explanation: You got it! The FSFI is the go-to tool researchers and clinicians use to measure things like desire, arousal, and comfort.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to holistic nursing practice in busy hospitals?

options.A: Hierarchical medical structures that limit nursing autonomy
options.B: Abundant staffing levels with too many nurses on every shift
options.C: Task-oriented routines focused only on quick medication rounds
options.D: Heavy workloads and high patient-to-nurse ratios

explanation: Great catch! Staff shortages and heavy workloads are major barriers in our hospitals, so abundant staffing is definitely not one of them.

question: What unit of measurement is commonly used to express energy expenditure in human nutrition?

options.A: Centimeters
options.B: Kilocalories
options.C: Milligrams
options.D: Milliliters

explanation: Energy in human nutrition is measured in kilocalories, which people commonly call calories. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h1)

question: What is the anatomical term for the neck region?

options.A: Thoracic
options.B: Cephalic
options.C: Cervical
options.D: Lumbar

explanation: The neck is anatomically referred to as the cervical region, linking the head to the chest. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of using BMI when assessing a very muscular athlete?

options.A: It consistently underestimates total body water volume
options.B: It cannot distinguish between heavy muscle mass and excess body fat
options.C: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate accurately
options.D: It only applies to children and cannot be used for adults

explanation: Correct! Because muscle is much heavier than fat, a fit athlete can show up as 'overweight' on a BMI chart even when they are very healthy.

question: Which opioid side effect requires preventative medication because the body never builds tolerance to it?

options.A: Nausea and vomiting
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Respiratory depression
options.D: Drowsiness and sedation

explanation: Tolerance develops to sedation and nausea over time, but the bowel remains sluggish, meaning constipation requires continuous preventative treatment. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h7)

question: What vital detail must you always include in your nursing notes when a patient passes away?

options.A: The total financial cost of hospital treatment
options.B: The exact time signs of death were observed
options.C: The personal religious beliefs of the nurse
options.D: The name of the nurse who takes over tomorrow

explanation: You got it! Recording the exact time is a legal must-do that shows when care transitioned and starts the paperwork.

question: What is the primary goal of microbial identification in a clinical setting?

options.A: To count the total number of human cells in a clinical sample
options.B: To measure the patient's exact blood pressure and pulse rate
options.C: To sterilize medical equipment before a surgical procedure
options.D: To determine the exact pathogen causing an infection for targeted treatment

explanation: Knowing the specific organism allows healthcare providers to choose the most effective and narrow-spectrum treatment possible. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h1)

question: What does it mean when a pathogen's 'portal of entry' matches its 'portal of exit'?

options.A: Infective hosts can only transmit diseases through surgical incisions
options.B: The route a pathogen uses to leave one host is often the same route it uses to enter another
options.C: Germs must always enter the bloodstream before they are capable of leaving the body
options.D: Pathogens change their shape completely when moving from one person to another

explanation: It's all about matching pathways. Many germs love to enter and leave the body using the exact same system, like the nose/mouth respiratory tract or the gut.

question: What is your main responsibility as a nurse when a new clinical policy is introduced?

options.A: To rewrite the entire hospital operating budget
options.B: To discard the policy if it takes too much time
options.C: To report the hospital board to the police
options.D: To integrate the new rules into daily clinical practice

explanation: As professional nurses, we adopt updated guidelines into our everyday care to make sure our practice stays safe and standardized.

question: What must be obtained from participants before data collection begins?

options.A: Proof of employment
options.B: A financial deposit
options.C: Physician resignation
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after fully understanding what the study involves. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h5)

question: A patient lies quietly with closed eyes, but opens them right away when you call their name loudly. What is their eye score?
explanation: Spot on! When they open their eyes only after you speak to them or call their name, that's a score of 3.

question: Why should patients always be involved in setting their own rehabilitation goals?

options.A: It ensures the recovery targets matter to the patient's actual daily life.
options.B: It completely removes the need for physical therapy oversight.
options.C: Hospital accreditation rules legally prohibit nurse-only care plans.
options.D: Patients have medical degrees that guide clinical interventions.

explanation: Exactly! When patients help choose what they want to achieve, they feel more motivated to push through tough therapy sessions.

question: What is the primary definition of maternal morbidity in nursing practice?

options.A: Any health condition resulting from or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: The permanent inability to conceive after experiencing a miscarriage
options.C: Any psychological stress experienced immediately after delivering a baby
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in a specific community

explanation: Maternal morbidity covers any physical or mental condition that affects a woman because of pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period, short of death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: A patient recovering from a stroke is coughing and clearing their throat frequently during meals. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Wait until the meal is finished before reporting the cough
options.B: Lie the patient flat on their back to ease breathing
options.C: Stop feeding immediately and assess for swallowing difficulties
options.D: Encourage the patient to drink more thin liquids quickly

explanation: Frequent coughing during eating is a major warning sign of aspiration, which can lead to severe pneumonia. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T4#GNS123_U6_T4_h3)

question: What type of immune reaction causes the raised bump during a Mantoux test?

options.A: Immediate antibody production
options.B: Complement system activation
options.C: Cell-mediated hypersensitivity
options.D: Innate inflammatory defense

explanation: Think of this as your immune cells (T-cells) rushing to the spot and throwing a little party that takes a day or two to show up as a firm lump! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h2)

question: What is participatory management in nursing administration?

options.A: Allowing patients to write their own medication prescriptions
options.B: Leaving all hospital decisions entirely to government ministers
options.C: Involving staff nurses in decision-making processes like shift planning
options.D: Banning staff meetings to save time during busy shifts

explanation: Participatory management means management doesn't just bark orders; they bring nurses into the conversation when making decisions that affect the ward.

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who just received IV contrast dye?

options.A: Stay strictly in bed for the next two days
options.B: Take a strong antibiotic pill
options.C: Avoid eating any protein for the rest of the day
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush the dye out

explanation: Drinking water helps the kidneys wash the contrast dye out of the body quickly and safely.

question: How does the body get rid of extra fluid from the skin and tissues right after birth?

options.A: Through rapid shedding of the top layer of skin cells
options.B: By reabsorbing all fluid directly back into the digestive tract
options.C: Through heavy postpartum sweating and increased urination
options.D: By storing extra fluid permanently in the muscle tissue

explanation: Sweating buckets and frequent bathroom trips are your body's clever ways of clearing out all that extra pregnancy fluid!

question: Which underlying societal belief most drives the practice of breast ironing?

options.A: Believing large breasts cause chronic back pain in women
options.B: Expecting all young girls to participate in military service

options.D: Requiring women to alter their bodies for traditional marriage

question: What is one of the most important roles of a nurse in a pediatric care team?

options.A: Performing surgeries independently
options.B: Diagnosing genetic conditions without lab tests
options.C: Deciding when the child needs major surgery
options.D: Coordinating care and bridging communication between family and specialists

explanation: Nurses are the heartbeat of the healthcare team! Because you spend the most time with the family, you help tie all the specialist care together.

question: What actually drives water to move passively across the wall of the intestine?

options.A: Active water pumps on the enterocyte membrane
options.B: Changes in core body temperature
options.C: Direct muscle contractions of the villi
options.D: Osmotic gradients created by solute absorption

explanation: Water loves to follow the crowd! As the gut pumps in salts and sugars, water naturally flows right along with them through osmosis.

question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

options.A: It only affects travellers visiting from foreign countries
options.B: It appears once every ten years and then vanishes
options.C: It is constantly present at a steady baseline level
options.D: It suddenly affects people across multiple continents

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as a constant visitor—it stays within a specific area consistently over time without needing a fresh introduction from outside. You've got this!

question: Why must a nurse leader look at all four parts of Deming's framework together?

options.A: Because licensing boards force you to recite all four terms in patient charts
options.B: Because treating them separately will crash the hospital computers
options.C: Because the four components overlap and deeply influence one another in real practice
options.D: Because focusing on just one part is illegal in healthcare

explanation: They work best as a team! Understanding people (psychology), systems, variation, and theory all blend together when solving daily ward challenges.

question: Why must nurses always take complaints of menstrual pain seriously?

options.A: It is a legal requirement to report menstrual cramps to public health boards
options.B: Severe pain always indicates an underlying malignant tumour in the uterus
options.C: Menstrual pain is often dismissed despite being disabling for the patient
options.D: Pain during menstruation is extremely rare and requires immediate surgery

explanation: You got it! People often brush off menstrual cramps as 'normal,' so as nurses, our validation and compassionate care make a real difference.

question: Why can missing certain body enzymes lead to cell damage when taking a drug?

options.A: They allow the drug to pass through the kidneys too quickly
options.B: They create toxic byproducts that harm internal cell structures
options.C: They stop the stomach from absorbing the medication entirely
options.D: They cause the heart rate to drop dangerously low within minutes

question: Why is an MRI generally considered safer than a CT scan regarding radiation?

options.A: It exposes the body to much lower doses of standard X-rays
options.B: It completely avoids interacting with any atoms inside the human body
options.C: It requires the patient to take a protective oral medication first
options.D: It uses radiofrequency and magnetic fields instead of ionizing radiation

explanation: Spot on! Because an MRI doesn't use ionizing radiation, it's a much safer choice for avoiding radiation exposure.

question: When does tertiary prevention come into play during the course of an illness?

options.A: Before any risk factors are present in the community
options.B: During routine health promotion and wellness talks
options.C: After disease and complications have already occurred
options.D: When conducting mass screening tests for healthy adults

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in when a disease is already established, focusing on helping the patient recover and manage life.

question: Why does a person with iron deficiency anemia look so pale?

options.A: Lack of iron thickens the outer layer of the skin
options.B: Poor circulation causes blood to pool exclusively in deep organs
options.C: Reduced hemoglobin levels decrease the red color of the blood and skin
options.D: The liver stops producing melanin pigments in the skin

explanation: Correct! Hemoglobin is what gives blood its bright red color. When iron is low, hemoglobin drops, and the skin loses that healthy pinkish glow. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h4)

question: Which medication is the specific emergency reversal antidote for a heparin overdose?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Naloxone hydrochloride
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Protamine sulfate

explanation: Protamine sulfate is heparin's best counter-punch. It binds right to heparin and neutralizes it almost instantly if bleeding gets out of hand.

question: Why can a brain abscess cause symptoms that look just like a brain tumor?

options.A: It acts as a mass that takes up space and increases pressure inside the skull.
options.B: It causes the hair on the scalp to fall out rapidly.
options.C: It replaces normal brain cells with cancer cells.
options.D: It changes the genetic makeup of surrounding neurons over time.

explanation: A pocket of pus inside the head takes up physical space, just like a tumor. This raises the pressure inside the skull (ICP) and presses on nearby brain areas.

question: A nurse is assessing an eight-month-old infant at a primary health clinic. Which measurement should be taken to monitor normal brain growth?

options.A: Mid-upper arm size
options.B: Crown-to-heel length
options.C: Head circumference

question: How should you position your patient right after a thoracentesis is finished?

options.A: On the unaffected side
options.B: Prone on the abdomen
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: Flat on the affected side

question: What is the medical term when a patient is taking multiple medications all at once?

options.A: Polypharmacy
options.B: Anaphylaxis
options.C: Idiosyncrasy
options.D: Pharmacovigilance

question: What does the Infant Mortality Rate measure?

options.A: Babies who die before reaching their first birthday
options.B: Children under five years old who get malaria
options.C: Mothers who die during childbirth
options.D: Total number of babies born in a hospital

question: A patient calls a few days post-surgery with a high fever and worsening belly pain. What should you advise?

options.A: Perform strenuous exercises to sweat out the fever
options.B: Return to the hospital promptly for medical evaluation
options.C: Eat a large heavy meal to restore body energy levels
options.D: Take an extra sleeping pill and wait until next week

explanation: You got it! Fever and worsening pain are warning signs of infection or internal injury, so the patient needs to be checked at the hospital right away.

question: When should you refer a post-abortion client to a mental health specialist?

options.A: When the client shows signs of severe depression or suicidal thoughts
options.B: Whenever the client has a mild headache
options.C: Every single time a client asks for a prescription for pain medicine
options.D: Only when the client refuses to take iron tablets

explanation: While basic emotional support is part of everyday nursing, deep psychological distress, severe depression, or self-harm threats need expert psychiatric help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: A patient complains that fresh vegetables are too expensive for their weekly budget. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Insist that only imported fresh produce will help their condition
options.B: Suggest nutritious and affordable frozen or local seasonal options
options.C: Advise the patient to borrow money to buy groceries
options.D: Tell the patient to stop eating vegetables altogether

explanation: Wonderful clinical intuition! Always help patients find budget-friendly, local alternatives so they can stay healthy without breaking the bank. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: What should the nurse do immediately upon discovering a cracked jaw on a hemostat during preparation?

options.A: Return it to the standard surgical tray without telling anyone
options.B: Remove the instrument from service and report the damage
options.C: Apply strong glue to the crack before sending it to autoclave
options.D: Use it only for minor tasks away from deep organs

question: Which gas law explains why trapped air inside a patient's body expands as an aircraft climbs?

options.A: Dalton's Law

options.D: Boyle's Law

question: Which group of complementary therapies includes herbal remedies and natural dietary supplements?

options.A: Mind-body interventions
options.B: Whole medical systems
options.C: Energy therapies
options.D: Biologically based practices

question: What is the main role of a nurse when a patient is referred for genetic counseling?

options.A: Prescribing gene-therapy medications to correct mutations
options.B: Providing the final diagnosis for the genetic disorder
options.C: Preparing the patient emotionally and clarifying basic hereditary concepts

question: What is the main task of cytotoxic T-cells?

options.A: Producing free-floating antibodies in the blood plasma
options.B: Destroying infected or cancerous body cells directly
options.C: Filtering waste materials out of the lymphatic fluid

question: Which muscle group forms the main support sling at the base of the pelvis?

question: Which of these should you NEVER do when handling hospital disinfectants?

question: What is a major economic barrier to healthcare access for many low-income families in Nigeria?

options.A: An excessive abundance of free community health centers

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever after drinking fresh, unpasteurized milk from a family farm. What is the most likely source of infection?

question: Which patient in a busy emergency ward should a nurse monitor with a pulse oximeter first?

question: What does 'anticipatory grief' mean?

options.C: Mourning that only affects family members rather than patients
options.D: A sudden emotional breakdown with no clear identifiable trigger

question: What does the term 'tolerance' mean when someone takes sleeping pills for a long time?

options.A: The drug stays active in the bloodstream for a shorter duration

options.C: The patient experiences allergic skin rashes after repeated use

question: What is the primary reason harmful traditional practices persist in many communities?

options.A: Mandates from international health bodies

question: What does the Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (CPR) actually tell us?

question: What is the main goal of doing an anthropometric assessment in nursing?

options.A: Measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the body

question: What is the main goal of genetic counseling for couples in communities with high sickle cell rates?

question: When were the very first official Recommended Dietary Allowances introduced?
